fun.reason: Hit rate per throw is 0.58 to 0.69, so most throws pay off, but the opening-mover edge (red wins 59% in 2v2, 65% in 3v3 on the engine) and 12 to 17 rounds per team match make the middle of a match feel long and partly pre-decided.

fairness.reason: The engine's fixed opener wins 65% in 3v3, and in 1v1 the knight loses 73.7% of its matches to skeleton (skeleton beats knight 73.7%); the page build shows an even worse hero skew (bride 20% and hunchback 23% as left lead vs wizard 73%).

tension.reason: Comeback tools fire 9.0 to 16.2 times per match and pity 4.7 to 6.5 times, so deficits are rarely final, but the stacked multiplier of up to 2.3x, with near-misses hitting from 450 px away, makes the swings feel automatic rather than earned.

pacing.reason: Team matches average 12.1 rounds (2v2) and 17.5 rounds (3v3), but the ramp starts at round 13, so 2v2 is nearly over before any acceleration and 3v3 gets only about 5 ramp rounds; the 3v3 p10 to p90 spread is 16 to 19.

team_play.reason: Only one thrower acts per team per round, so 3v3 means 17.5 rounds for about 3 units, and nothing in the data shows that unit choice, focus-fire or sequencing matters; the engine opener advantage (65% 3v3) is a bigger driver.

replayability.reason: 8 heroes and mixed teams give variety, but the 1v1 matrix (e.g. knight 26% vs skeleton, wizard 38% vs bat) and the strength gap deciding 92.9% of +2 matches shrink the set of viable picks; no team-run data exists to show team variety.

top_weaknesses: Team matches run 12.1 (2v2) and 17.5 (3v3) rounds versus 8.8 for 1v1, so a 3v3 is about 2x a duel and the 7-minute target is likely blown by roughly 2x unless a round takes under about 24 seconds.
The opener advantage is large in the engine: left wins 58.8% in 2v2 and 65.0% in 3v3, a 15-point structural edge before skill, which is not the accepted skill gap and needs a fix.
The ramp starts at round 13 while 2v2 averages 12.1 rounds, so it almost never triggers in 2v2 and cannot shorten 3v3 (p10 is 16 rounds, ramp covers only 3 to 6 rounds).

The 1v1 matrix has hard counters: skeleton beats knight 73.7%, and bride has 65.3% vs reaper and 62.7% vs hunchback while hunchback is at 39.7% against knight; the matrix spread of about 26% to 74% is too wide for a game where picks should matter but not decide.

The page build and the engine disagree on hero strength: bride wins 46.7% as left lead in the engine vs 20.0% on the page, hunchback 40.0% vs 23.3%, wizard 43.3% vs 73.3%, so at least one build has a drift bug and no hero stat can be trusted.

Comeback layering is heavy: pity (+0.4 per miss, cap 1.6), underdog (up to +1.0) and near-miss (450 px reach, 0.9 scale) can reach 2.3x, and 15 to 16 comeback hits per 3v3 match suggests a high share of damage comes from the safety net rather than from aim.

Strength gap is decisive: left wins 92.9% at +2 and only 27.3% at -2 in the engine, and a 3v3 with random hidden opponents may feel decided by matchmaking more than play (accepted by the owner, but it caps the achievable fairness score).
There is no data for seconds per round, human play, or any team run (team_simulation_runs is empty), so the 7-minute goal and the team tuning are unverified.

to_reach_10.change: Cut 3v3 and 2v2 match length by lowering team HP and moving the ramp earlier
to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: hp_scale 2v2 from 0.9 to 0.70, 3v3 from 0.95 to 0.62; ramp start_round 13 to 7 (2v2) and 8 (3v3), per_round 0.08 to 0.12
to_reach_10.expected_effect: Rounds fall from 12.1 to about 8.5 (2v2) and from 17.5 to about 10.5 (3v3), close to the 1v1 mean of 8.8
to_reach_10.risk: Lower HP makes hits swingier and raises the opener's advantage unless the opener fix ships together

to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: Give the second-moving team +1 supply crate or +15% damage on its first throw, or alternate the first mover per round pair (R1 red, R2 blue throws first and second in a snake order); target left win rate 47 to 53% at both sizes
to_reach_10.risk: Alternating re-creates the old double-attack by the second mover if done per round instead of in a snake order

to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: knight dmg 21 to 24 and hp 185 to 175 (skeleton beats it 73.7%); hunchback dmg 19 to 22; bride dmg 34 to 31; wizard hp 124 to 130; re-run 300 matches per pairing and accept every cell between 40% and 60%
to_reach_10.expected_effect: Shrinks the matrix spread from 26 to 74% to about 38 to 62%
to_reach_10.risk: Hunchback and knight changes shift team value and can create a new outlier such as hag

to_reach_10.change: Find and fix the engine versus page hero skew
to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: Diff both builds on seeds 7 and 8 with identical hero tables; require left-lead hero win rates to agree within 8 points (today bride 46.7 vs 20.0, wizard 43.3 vs 73.3)
to_reach_10.expected_effect: Removes a hidden bug so every other balance number becomes trustworthy
to_reach_10.risk: If it is not a bug but a difference in the AI, the AI itself needs a shared policy

to_reach_10.change: Thin the comeback stack so aim still matters
to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: cap the total multiplier at 1.8 (from 2.3), pity per_miss 0.4 to 0.25 and cap 1.6 to 1.0, near-miss reach_px 450 to 300 and scale 0.9 to 0.7
to_reach_10.expected_effect: Cuts comeback hits from 9.0 to 16.2 per match to about 5 to 9, so a lead is worth more
to_reach_10.risk: If the opener fix is missing, weaker comebacks let the engine's 65% edge grow

to_reach_10.change: Make team play a real decision so team_play can move off 5
to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: allow the thrower to be chosen each round from living units (no repeating the same unit twice in a row), add a +20% damage bonus when a different hero hits the same enemy within 2 consecutive rounds, and an ultimate pip bonus of 1 for a kill
to_reach_10.expected_effect: Adds focus-fire and rotation decisions, and a kill gets a reward so that finishing a unit is not the same as chipping
to_reach_10.risk: More options slow a turn, so seconds per round go up and eat part of the 7-minute gain

to_reach_10.change: Measure time and rebuild the 7-minute target from seconds
to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: Log seconds per round for bots and 20 real players, then set rounds_target = 420 / seconds_per_round; at 25 s per round that is 17 rounds, at 40 s it is 10.5
to_reach_10.expected_effect: Turns the 7-minute goal into an exact round budget instead of a guess
to_reach_10.risk: Real players take much longer than bots on aiming, which could force the target under 8 rounds

to_reach_10.change: Run 300 matches per end for team sizes and report win rate by hero pair, by opener and by team composition
to_reach_10.concrete_numbers: 2v2 and 3v3, 300 matches each, report win rate per hero in team (target 42 to 58%), per opener (target 47 to 53%), round p90 at or below target plus 2
to_reach_10.expected_effect: Fills the empty team_simulation_runs and makes the team ratings measurable
to_reach_10.risk: If the team-only numbers diverge from the 240-match matrix, the tuning in change 1 needs a second pass

seven_minute_plan.rounds_target: About 10 rounds for 3v3 and 8 for 2v2, assuming about 40 s per round including aiming, animation and ultimates (420 s / 40 s is 10.5); if the real figure is 25 s the target is 17 rounds, which is close to today's 17.5, so the first task is to measure seconds per round
seven_minute_plan.hp_scale: 2v2: 0.70, 3v3: 0.62, with hp_floor_hits kept at 2.5 so no unit dies in fewer than 2.5 average hits
seven_minute_plan.ramp_start_round: Round 7 for 2v2 and round 8 for 3v3 with per_round 0.12, so damage reaches about +50% by round 11 and hard-ends stalemates
seven_minute_plan.round_cap: 2v2: 12 (from 24), 3v3: 14 (from 28), with a tie-break by HP share at the cap; today round_cap fired 0 times, so the cap is a safety net and the real control is HP scale and ramp
seven_minute_plan.reasoning: Current means of 12.1 and 17.5 rounds are driven by team HP that is almost the same as 1v1 per unit (0.9 and 0.95 of full) while only one thrower acts per round, so total HP is 1.8x to 2.85x a duel. Cutting HP scale to 0.70 and 0.62 gives total HP of about 1.4x and 1.9x a duel, which at 0.58 to 0.69 hits per throw lands near 8.5 and 10.5 rounds. The ramp must start before the average match ends (round 13 does not), so it moves to round 7 to 8. All of this is an estimate: with no seconds per round and no team simulation run, the 7-minute claim stays unproven until both are measured.

cannot_judge: Seconds per round, so the 7-minute conversion from rounds is impossible
How the game feels to real people: every number is from computer-controlled matches, so the actual fun, frustration and the feel of comeback hits are unknown
Whether the hidden random opponent strength creates matches that feel unfair to a human even when the numbers say they are balanced
Team composition effects: team_simulation_runs is empty, so no pair or trio synergy, no worst team and no hero pick rate is available
Which build (engine or page) is the source of truth, since the left-lead hero results disagree by up to 45 points
Whether the 21 of 3528 bride shots fixed earlier changed the bride's real win rate, because the matrix was measured partly after rebalancing and partly before
Visual, audio and UI quality, onboarding, and retention over days, none of which a simulation can show
